takes.h: The Return of the Living Dead sequel casts Johnny Knoxville and Doug Jones
takes.p: Dread Central, citing Deadline, reports Johnny Knoxville, Doug Jones, Sean Gunn, Ruby Snowber and Blake Richardson are set to star in filmmaker Steve Wolsh's direct sequel to Dan O'Bannon's 1985 film, set in 1984. Tony Gardner is overseeing the zombie designs, and shooting is planned for the spring.

takes.h: Robert McCammon named Monsterama 2027 Grandmaster Guest of Honor
takes.p: Robert McCammon's official site reports he is Monsterama's 2027 Grandmaster Guest of Honor. The Atlanta-area convention runs August 6–8, 2027, at the Atlanta Marriott Northeast/Emory Hotel, with the theme “The Magic of Stop-Motion Animation.” Caroline Munro, Martine Beswick, Patrick Wayne and Kurt Christian are also named guests.

takes.h: Pre-orders open for S.H. MonsterArts King Ghidorah from Godzilla Minus Zero
takes.p: The Toyark reports pre-orders opened for Tamashii Nations' S.H. MonsterArts King Ghidorah (2026) from Godzilla Minus Zero. The figure stands over 9.5 inches, measures nearly 27 inches from head to tail, and includes replacement wing parts and a dedicated stand. The Toyark lists an expected July 2027 release.

takes.h: Academy Museum sets The House of Horror: Hammer Films 1955–1974
takes.p: Dread Central, citing Variety, reports the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures will run The House of Horror: Hammer Films 1955–1974 from January 15 to 30. Listed screenings include The Curse of Frankenstein in 4K on January 17, The Plague of the Zombies on January 21 and The Vampire Lovers on January 28.

takes.h: Steve Miner's Jason wraps, dated for August 13, 2027
takes.p: JoBlo, citing Deadline, reports that the new Friday the 13th film is titled Jason and was wrapping production, with a worldwide theatrical release set for August 13, 2027. Schuyler White plays Jason and Natalie Alyn Lind plays Lauren. David Fliegel wrote the script; Cineverse distributes in North America.

takes.h: Warner's rival A Nightmare on Elm Street film is off
takes.p: A Warner Bros. Nightmare on Elm Street film, with Lee Cronin in talks to write and direct, is no longer moving forward, iHorror reports, citing Dread Central's Brad Miska. Paramount, which completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on October 6, is developing its own film from Wes Craven's original 1984 screenplay.

takes.h: Lividian sets shipping for McCammon's Baal and Bethany's Sin
takes.p: Baal, Book 1 of Lividian Publications' Robert McCammon Library, is open for preorder and shipping in late November, the press's production update says. Book 2, Bethany's Sin, is set to ship in late December; The Night Boat, They Thirst, Mystery Walk and Usher's Passing are in production for 2027.
